name: Kiro
description: Agentic IDE from AWS built on a VS Code-style editor, using a spec-driven workflow. Amazon Q Developer's IDE capabilities are migrating into it. Ships an MCP client, auto-triggering agent hooks, steering files, and a CLI.
abuse_potential: Three stacked execution primitives. Agent hooks fire the agent automatically on file events with no user action, and both hooks and MCP config are project-scoped under .kiro/ so they travel with a git clone. MCP entries carry an autoApprove array naming tools that run without confirmation. Config hot-reloads via a file watcher, so a tampered config takes effect without a restart and without the user reopening anything.

disk.description: User-scope MCP servers, applied across every workspace. Powers installed from the server directory are auto-registered here under a Powers section.
Workspace-scope MCP servers. TRAVELS WITH THE REPO - a clone or PR can introduce servers that launch on open.

JSON hook definitions. The when block sets the trigger (fileSaved, fileCreated, fileDeleted, manual, prompt and agent lifecycle events, spec task events) with a file pattern; the then block invokes the agent with a prompt. A fileSaved hook is an AUTO-TRIGGERING EXECUTION PRIMITIVE that needs no user interaction. Enumerate every hook during triage.
Markdown guidance loaded selectively into agent context, optionally with 'inclusion: auto' frontmatter. Prompt-injection surface; travels with repo.
Agent configuration directory. Agents can define MCP servers inline, so this is a second location where servers are declared. Watched for hot-reload.
Spec-driven workflow artifacts (requirements, design, tasks). Useful for reconstructing what the agent was asked to build and when.
Kiro Power packages bundling MCP servers, skills, and steering. Installable from a remote repository, including private repos cloned locally.
MCP server stdout/stderr. Records connection attempts and failures - useful for establishing which servers actually ran.

name: Open WebUI
description: Self-hosted web interface for local and remote LLMs, formerly Ollama WebUI. Multi-user with RBAC, RAG document ingestion, and a Tools/Functions system that executes Python. Usually deployed via Docker; also installable via pip.
execution_model: Local or remote inference, self-hosted multi-user server
abuse_potential: The first account registered on a fresh instance is automatically the administrator, so an instance reachable before its owner registers can be taken over outright by whoever signs up first. Tools and Functions execute Python server-side. The OpenAI router exposes a catch-all proxy that forwards requests upstream using the admin-configured API key, turning an authenticated account into free use of the organisation's inference spend. Multiple RCE, SSRF, and information-disclosure CVEs have shipped against it.

disk.description: Root of all persistent state. DATA_DIR relocates it. If the volume was never mounted, all state lives in the container's writable layer and is lost on recreation - check before concluding data was deleted.

Auto-generated JWT signing key, written here when WEBUI_SECRET_KEY is not set in the environment and reloaded on restart.

Persisted application config. Note the tiered config model - database settings override environment variables unless ENABLE_PERSISTENT_CONFIG is false, so the running config may not match the env you were shown.
RAG document uploads and embedding store. Scope data exposure here - users commonly upload internal documents.
Deployment env file. Commonly holds WEBUI_SECRET_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, OLLAMA_BASE_URL, and WEBUI_ADMIN_PASSWORD in plaintext.
Records port mapping, volume mounts, and env injection. Establishes whether the instance was network-exposed and whether state was persisted.

collection.guidance: Snapshot the whole DATA_DIR volume before touching the container - recreating a container without the volume destroys everything. webui.db is the priority artifact; it carries chats, users, API keys, and stored Python in one file. If .webui_secret_key may have been read, rotate it and force re-authentication.

name: OpenHands
description: Autonomous software-engineering agent (formerly OpenDevin) with a web UI, running agent code in Docker sandbox containers. Deployed via Docker, Docker Compose, or from source.
execution_model: Cloud or local inference + sandboxed exec
abuse_potential: The documented run command mounts /var/run/docker.sock into the container - that is host-root-equivalent, so an agent or an attacker reaching the container controls the Docker daemon and therefore the host. Port 3000 has no authentication in the default local deployment.
